claims.statement: ConversationSaver persists a graph checkpoint before appending its message revisions to the independent archive and acknowledging the archive checkpoint; there is no cross-store transaction, archive failures propagate for repair, and idempotent archive revisions avoid duplicates on retry.

ConversationSaver shields checkpoint/archive writes from cancellation until both finish, then re-raises cancellation, while its shared lock prevents reset or deletion from racing an incomplete append.

Only root graph checkpoints with trusted Talon channel/chat metadata are eligible for transcript archival; unscoped and nested graph writes are excluded, and archive session registration prevents a session from being reassigned across chat scopes.

History vector indexes are separate from archive metadata, selected independently per storage scheme or exactly one vector plugin, and guarded by an embedding fingerprint; an incompatible retained index requires explicit reindexing that preserves transcripts and resumes progress after interruption.

The Talon README describes Talon as experimental, not intended for production or enterprise use, and lacking production-grade multi-tenant security boundaries; channel access should be treated as access to the operator's agent, credentials, tools, and local host resources.

DEEPAGENTS_TALON_CHECKPOINT_URI selects built-in SQLite/file, PostgreSQL, or MongoDB checkpointers, or exactly one checkpoint-backend entry-point plugin; checkpointer initialization errors are sanitized into configuration errors to avoid exposing URI credentials.

Checkpoint backend selection is independent from history backend selection; the default checkpointer is the assistant-local SQLite path, whereas remote checkpoint thread IDs are not automatically namespaced by assistant ID and changing the URI does not migrate checkpoint data.

DeepAgents uses a DeltaChannel for the messages state with snapshots every 50 updates; its reducer relies on LangGraph-assigned stable message IDs and deterministically replaces, removes, or resets messages during replay.

StateBackend is a thread-scoped virtual filesystem in LangGraph state: it reads fresh channel state and queues partial files-channel updates through LangGraph config keys, so writes are available in the current superstep and persist only with the graph's checkpoints.

StoreBackend stores file records in a caller-selected BaseStore namespace, persists across threads that share that namespace, and validates namespace components to prevent wildcard or glob injection; it may obtain the store from graph execution context or use an explicitly supplied store.

dcode stores local LangGraph session checkpoints in a hardened DEFAULT_STATE_DIR/sessions.db SQLite database; get_checkpointer supplies an ownership-fenced AsyncSqliteSaver, and thread discovery derives metadata from checkpoint rows with a covering index to avoid scanning checkpoint blobs.

dcode reconstructs a thread's visible message count from root-namespace messages writes when DeltaChannel snapshots omit the inline value, replaying writes in checkpoint/task/index order and including pending writes applied by a head-state read.

dcode local thread ownership uses per-thread operating-system file-lock reservations and random owner tokens; writer guards serialize mutations, reject a mismatched token or released client lease, and token rotation waits for an in-flight mutation before invalidating stale writers.

The ownership-aware SQLite saver fences checkpoint writes, pending writes, and deletion; deletion reserves an unowned thread for its duration, so a client cannot delete an open thread and cancellation does not release the reservation before cleanup completes.

RemoteAgent adds the current local ownership token to mutations and request headers while leaving reads unfenced; an externally managed server can disable that local ownership behavior with local_ownership=False.

dcode server startup generates a checkpointer configured with the local sessions database and ownership-fenced saver, then requires a project workspace and configures the RemoteAgent with its cwd, policy claim, and fingerprint.

RemoteAgent keeps workspace binding separate from checkpoint persistence: it configures workspace policy and fingerprint together, caches validated descriptors per thread, and idempotently registers remote thread records so persisted checkpoints can be mutated after a server restart.

dcode identifies pending graph work from queued nodes, tasks, or interrupts; abandoning it cancels active runs, writes error results only for dangling trailing-turn tool calls, ends the graph state, and verifies that work is cleared so stale tools are not executed on resume.

dcode thread deletion also removes separately persisted side-question costs and offloaded history after deleting SQLite checkpoint and write rows, so those records have a distinct lifecycle from graph checkpoints.
dcode generates new thread identifiers as time-ordered full UUID7 strings while continuing to list legacy short hexadecimal thread IDs alongside them.

dcode persists thread names in the separate dcode_thread_names table, prefers that durable name over checkpoint metadata, and falls back to the latest root-checkpoint name for older stores; atomic conditional rename preserves an existing name when automatic naming races.

The built-in thread inspector is a read-only workflow: it opens a supported local sessions database with SQLite mode=ro, accepts only an exact or unique escaped prefix for a root-namespace thread, and reconstructs messages from the latest checkpoint plus pending writes or by replaying root writes with warnings on malformed records.

dcode title generation treats conversation content as untrusted: it sends only bounded visible human and AI text to a tool-free model with callbacks disabled, excludes internal, control, tool, and shell messages, and normalizes the response to the same safe one-line title constraints used for manual names.

The app runs thread-title generation asynchronously and persists an automatic result with only_if_unnamed, so a concurrently set title is retained; it also waits for model initialization to finish during cancellation before allowing the timeout or cancellation to escape.

save_thread_seed creates a local discovery checkpoint only when the thread has no existing local checkpoint, stamps agent and cwd metadata, and releases a lease it acquired if saving fails or finishes; subsequent conversation history remains owned by the connected agent.
